en.title: Security Advisory: Temporary Disruptions Due to PHP Vulnerability Mitigation
en.description: Maldives Digital Service (MDS), in coordination with the National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA), is implementing necessary security patches, vulnerability mitigation measures, and system hardening activities in response to recently…
en.body:
Maldives Digital Service (MDS), in coordination with the National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA), is implementing necessary security patches, vulnerability mitigation measures, and system hardening activities in response to recently identified critical vulnerabilities affecting PHP web technologies, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.

These proactive measures are being undertaken to address potential security risks, prevent unauthorized access, and strengthen the protection and resilience of government digital infrastructure and services.

The PHP development team has released security updates in PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12 to address these vulnerabilities, and affected systems are strongly advised to be updated immediately.

Temporary service disruptions may occur while these security measures are being implemented. MDS will work to minimize any impact and restore affected government digital services as quickly as possible.

MDS, in close coordination with NCSA, remains committed to strengthening national cybersecurity readiness and ensuring the continued security, reliability, and resilience of government digital services.

🛡️ Strengthening Cybersecurity. Securing Government Digital Services.

Read the official PHP Security Advisory from the link below.

🔗 [https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php)

featuredImage.alt: Bringing eFaas Support Closer to Communities: Mobile Helpdesk Sessions held in Hulhumalé

en.title: Bringing eFaas Support Closer to Communities: Mobile Helpdesk Sessions held in Hulhumalé
en.description: Maldives Digital Service (MDS), in collaboration with Housing Development Corporation (HDC), successfully conducted two eFaas Mobile Helpdesk sessions in Hulhumalé on 9 and 10 October 2026.The sessions were held at Hiyaa Park on 9 October…
en.body:
Maldives Digital Service (MDS), in collaboration with Housing Development Corporation (HDC), successfully conducted two eFaas Mobile Helpdesk sessions in Hulhumalé on 9 and 10 October 2026.The sessions were held at Hiyaa Park on 9 October and Central Park on 10 October, providing residents of Hulhumalé Phase 1 and Phase 2 with direct access to eFaas-related assistance and information.

During the two-day initiative, the MDS team assisted members of the public with eFaas registration, face verification, and other account-related queries and issues. The initiative forms part of MDS's continued efforts to strengthen public awareness and adoption of eFaas. By bringing support services directly to communities, MDS aims to make digital services more accessible and encourage greater public participation in the country's digital transformation.

Aligned with the government's Maldives 2.0 vision, the initiative supports ongoing efforts to modernize public service delivery and promote a more connected and digitally empowered nation. The sessions conducted in Hulhumalé follow similar awareness activities previously held in Kulhudhuffushi City and Dh. Kudahuvadhoo. MDS will continue expanding its public outreach efforts to improve awareness, accessibility, and adoption of eFaas across the Maldives.

dv.title: އީފާސްގެ އެހީތެރިކަން ރައްޔިތުންނާ ގާތަށް: މޯބައިލް ހެލްޕްޑެސްކް ސެޝަންތަކެއް ހުޅުމާލޭގައި ބާއްވައިފި
dv.description: މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް (އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް) އިން ހައުސިންގ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް ކޯޕަރޭޝަން (އެޗް.ޑީ.ސީ) އާ ގުޅިގެން، ކާމިޔާބުކަމާއެކު އީފާސް މޯބައިލް ހެލްޕްޑެސްކުގެ ދެ ސެޝަނެއް 2026 އޮކްޓޫބަރު 9 އަދި 10 ގައި ހުޅުމާލޭގައި ކުރިއަށް ގެންގޮސްފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް (އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް) އިން ހައުސިންގ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް ކޯޕަރޭޝަން (އެޗް.ޑީ.ސީ) އާ ގުޅިގެން، ކާމިޔާބުކަމާއެކު އީފާސް މޯބައިލް ހެލްޕްޑެސްކުގެ ދެ ސެޝަނެއް 2026 އޮކްޓޫބަރު 9 އަދި 10 ގައި ހުޅުމާލޭގައި ކުރިއަށް ގެންގޮސްފިއެވެ.

މި ސެޝަންތައް ބާއްވާފައިވަނީ އޮކްޓޫބަރު 9 ވަނަ ދުވަހު ހިޔާ ޕާކް އަދި އޮކްޓޫބަރު 10 ވަނަ ދުވަހު ސެންޓްރަލް ޕާކުގައެވެ. މި ސެޝަންތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ހުޅުމާލެ ފޭސް 1 އަދި ފޭސް 2 ގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އީފާސްއާ ގުޅުންހުރި އެހީތެރިކަމާއި މަޢުލޫމާތު ފަސޭހަކަމާއެކު ލިބިގެންދިޔައެވެ.

ދެ ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށް ކުރިއަށް ގެންދިޔަ މި ހަރަކާތުގައި، އީފާސް ރަޖިސްޓްރީ ކުރުމާއި، ފޭސް ވެރިފިކޭޝަން ހެދުމުގެ އިތުރުން އެކައުންޓާ ގުޅުންހުރި އެކި މައްސަލަތަކަށް އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް ގެ ޓީމުން ވަނީ އެހީތެރިކަން ފޯރުކޮށްދީފައެވެ. މި ހަރަކާތަކީ އީފާސްއަށް އާންމުން ހޭލުންތެރިކުރުވުމަށާއި، އީފާސް ބޭނުންކުރާ މިންވަރު އިތުރުކުރުމަށް އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް އިން ކުރަމުންދާ މަސައްކަތްތަކުގެ ތެރެއިން ބޭއްވުނު ހަރަކާތެކެވެ. ރައްޔިތުންނާއި ހަމައަށް މިފަދަ ޚިދުމަތްތައް ސީދާ ގެނެސްދިނުމުގެ ބޭނުމަކީ، ޑިޖިޓަލް ޚިދުމަތްތައް ފަސޭހަކަމާއެކު ލިބޭނެ މަގު ފަހިކޮށްދިނުމުގެ އިތުރުން، ރާއްޖޭގެ ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަންގައި އާންމުންގެ ބައިވެރިވުން އިތުރުކުރުމެވެ.

ސަރުކާރުގެ "މޯލްޑިވްސް 2.0" ތަސައްވުރުގެ ތެރެއިން ހިންގުނު މި ހަރަކާތަކީ އާންމު ޚިދުމަތްތައް ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުން ޒަމާނީ ކުރުމަށާއި، ޑިޖިޓަލް ގޮތުން ބާރުވެރި ޤައުމެއް ބިނާކުރުމަށް ކުރެވެމުންދާ މަސައްކަތްތަކުގެތެރެއިން ކުރެވުނު މުހިއްމު މަސައްކަތެކެވެ.

ހުޅުމާލޭގައި މި ބޭއްވުނު ސެޝަންތަކަކީ މީގެ ކުރިން ކުޅުދުއްފުށި ސިޓީ އަދި ދ. ކުޑަހުވަދޫގައި ވެސް ކުރިއަށް ގެންދެވުނު މިފަދަ ހޭލުންތެރިކުރުމުގެ ހަރަކާތްތަކުގެ ކުރިއެރުމެކެވެ. މުޅި ރާއްޖޭގައި އީފާސްއަށް އޮތް ހޭލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރުކުރުމަށާއި، ޚިދުމަތް ފަސޭހައިން ލިބޭނެ މަގު ތަނަވަސްކޮށް، އީފާސް ބޭނުންކުރާ ފަރާތްތަކުގެ އަދަދު އިތުރުކުރުމަށްޓަކައި އާންމުންނަށް އަމާޒުކޮށްގެން ހިންގާ މިފަދަ މަސައްކަތްތައް އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް އިން ކުރިއަށް އޮތްތަނުގައި ވެސް ފުޅާކުރަމުން ގެންދާނެއެވެ.

featuredImage.alt: Maldives Digital Summit 2026 Concludes with a Strong Call to Action for a Digital First Nation

en.title: Maldives Digital Summit 2026 Concludes with a Strong Call to Action for a Digital First Nation
en.description: Malé, Republic of Maldives | 30 th April 2026 The Maldives Digital Summit 2026, held from 27–29 April 2026 at Barceló Nasandhura Hotel, has successfully concluded after three days of high-level dialogue, technical workshops, and practical…
en.body:
Malé, Republic of Maldives | 30th April 2026

The Maldives Digital Summit 2026, held from 27–29 April 2026 at Barceló Nasandhura Hotel, has successfully concluded after three days of high-level dialogue, technical workshops, and practical collaboration. The summit reaffirmed the Maldives’ commitment to the Maldives 2.0 Vision: building a resilient, inclusive, and Digital First Nation.

**Opening Ceremony and Remarks**

The Summit commenced with the recitation of the Holy Quran by Mr. Aayan Ahmed Inaan, a student at Villa International High School.

The Summit was officially inaugurated by Mr. Ali Ihusaan, Minister of Homeland Security, Labour and Technology. In his address, he outlined the Maldives 2.0 Vision and the nation’s digital transformation roadmap also emphasized people‑centered digital public infrastructure, whole government coordination, secure and interoperable data sharing, trusted digital identity as well as the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Opening remarks were also delivered by Ms. Vyjayanti Desai, Practice Manager for Digital & AI, South Asia Region, World Bank. In her address, she highlighted the World Bank’s Digital Strategy and its engagement with the Maldives through the D’MADD Project, underscoring the importance of data-driven governance, digital public infrastructure and institutional capacity building.

**Global Perspectives on Digital Transformation**

The Summit featured Country Spotlight sessions showcasing international digital transformation journeys and these sessions provided valuable global perspectives for the implementation of Maldives 2.0.

1.

Dr. Yoon-seok Ko, Vice President of the National Information Society Agency (South Korea), shared Korea’s milestones, priorities, challenges, and lessons learned.

2.

Mr. Iurie Turcanu, former Deputy Prime Minister for Digitalization of Moldova, shared on Moldova’s digital evolution and success factors.

3.

Ms. Jessica McEvoy, Director of Delivery, Apolitical, Former Deputy Director, Platforms & Services, Government Digital Service, United Kingdom, presented insights from the United Kingdom’s digital transformation experience.

**Pannel Discussions and Policy Dialogue**

A central highlight was the high‑level panel “Implementing Maldives 2.0: Building a Digital First Nation through a Global Lens”, moderated by Ms. Anna Metz, Digital Transformation Specialist, World Bank. The discussion explored the best practices of the global, cross‑government collaboration, capacity building as well as the role of the private sector in enabling national digital transformation.

**Panelists:**

1.

Dr. Mohamed Kinaanath, Minister of State for Homeland Security, Labour and Technology & Head of Maldives Digital Service

2.

Ms. Saeeda Umar, Managing Director, MINDCo

3.

Dr. Yoon‑seok Ko, Vice President of the National Information Society Agency, South Korea

4.

Mr. Iurie Turcanu, former Deputy Prime Minister for Digitalization, Moldova

5.

Ms. Jessica McEvoy, Director of Delivery, Apolitical, Former Deputy Director, Platforms & Services, Government Digital Service, United Kingdom

Another key panel, “Mobilizing for Government Digital Transformation: Action Plan for Maldives 2.0”, was moderated by Mr. Hussain Naushad, Senior Government Digital Service Specialist, MDS. The session stressed coordinated action, safeguards, and stakeholder engagement to ensure meaningful digital transformation.

**Panelists:**

1.

Mr. Ahmed Shafeeu, Minister of State for Education, Higher Education and Skills Development

2.

Ms. Shazra Mohamed Saeed, Project Manager, Maldives Digital Service

3.

Ms. Aminath Ahlaam, Manager, Strategic Planning & Projects, MINDCo

4.

Mr. Mohamed Riznee, Director General, National Cybersecurity Agency

5.

Mr. Abdulla Muizz Ahmed, Deputy Director General – IT, Ministry of Health, Family and Welfare

**Strengthening Data, Cybersecurity, and Digital Infrastructure**

Key technical sessions addressed the foundations of digital government. These discussions were complemented by interactive technical dialogues that produced mini action plans for the Maldives Data Exchange (MDX).

1.

Mr. Hussain Naushad, Senior Government Digital Service Specialist, Maldives Digital Service, presented on data sharing enablers and digital infrastructure.

2.

Mr. Ahmed Naufal Abdul Hadee, Chief Executive Officer, National Cybersecurity Agency, highlighted cybersecurity considerations for data sharing.

3.

A panel on government data sharing good practices, moderated by Ms. Anna Metz, Digital Transformation Specialist, World Bank, featured:

o Dr. Yoon-seok Ko, Vice President of the National Information Society Agency, South Korea

o Mr. Iurie Turcanu, former Deputy Prime Minister for Digitalization, Moldova

o Mr. Hassaan Mohamed, Chief Executive Officer, Environmental Regulatory Authority

o Mr. Aditya Agrawal, Founder & Chief Executive Officer, D4DInsights

o Mr. Hany Nasyr, Senior Software Engineer, Maldives Digital Service

**Service Design, AI, and Emerging Technologies**

1.

Mr. Mohamed Arushad, Lead Solutions Engineer, MINDCo, presented on Maldives’ evolving vision for service design.

2.

Ms. Jessica McEvoy, Director of Delivery, Apolitical; former Deputy Director, Platforms & Services, Government Digital Service, UK, delivered sessions on UK Service Design Principles and led a Service Design Masterclass.

3.

Panel on citizen-centric service design, moderated by Mr. Mohamed Ushau, Head of Future Institute, MINDCo, featured:

o Ms. Jessica McEvoy, Director of Delivery, Apolitical, Former Deputy Director, Platforms & Services, Government Digital Service, UK

o Mr. Mohamed Arushad, Lead Solutions Engineer, MINDCo

o Mr. Hany Nasyr, Senior Software Engineer, Maldives Digital Service

o Mr. Abdulla Musthafa, CTO, Payment Maldives

o Mr. Ibrahim Mohamed, Executive Director, Bridging the Communities Maldives

4.

Dr. Ibrahim Shiyam, Minister of State for homeland Security, labour and technology, presented how MDS is leveraging AI for policy drafting and governance.

5.

Dr. Yoon-seok Ko shared South Korea’s experience using AI to strengthen digital government.

6.

Mr. Mohamed Ushau presented Building National Shared AI Capability on behalf of MINDCo.

**Inclusion, Digital Identity, and Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) Modernization**

1.

Women in Tech Maldives Panel: Inclusive by Design, moderated by Ms. Fathimath Zameela, emphasized accessibility and inclusive digital services.

2.

Sessions on digital wallets, verifiable credentials, e-signatures, and eFaas upgrades featured Ms. Anna Metz, Mr. Iurie Turcanu, and Ms. Shazra Mohamed Saeed.

3.

CRVS and National ID modernization sessions included:

o Mr. Mohamed Umair, Director, Department of National Registration

o Ms. Moomina Abdullah, Deputy Director General, Ministry of Health

o Ms. Aishath Hassan, Chief Statistician, Maldives Bureau of Statistics

**Contributors and Participants**

Throughout the Summit, contributors and participants include, DNR, MDS, MINDCo, NCSA, Health sector, Education sector, financial sector, Digital Transformation Officers from key government agencies, technology professionals, and global experts.

**Closing Ceremony**

The Summit concluded with closing remarks by Dr. Mohamed Kinaanath, Minister of State for Homeland Security, Labour and Technology and Head of MDS, reflecting on collective progress and reinforcing the importance of sustained collaboration and coordinated implementation as well as Ms. Anna Metz (World Bank) delivered closing reflections, highlighting partnership, shared learning, and continued collaboration.

featuredImage.alt: Maldives Digital Summit 2026 to Drive the Nation’s Digital-First Transformation Agenda

en.title: Maldives Digital Summit 2026 to Drive the Nation’s Digital-First Transformation Agenda
en.description: The Maldives Digital Service (MDS), under the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology, in collaboration with the World Bank, will convene the Maldives Digital Summit 2026 from 27 th to 29 th April 2026 at the Barceló Nasandhura Hotel,…
en.body:
The Maldives Digital Service (MDS), under the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology, in collaboration with the World Bank, will convene the Maldives Digital Summit 2026 from 27th to 29th April 2026 at the Barceló Nasandhura Hotel, Malé. The summit represents a major milestone in advancing the Maldives 2.0 Vision: The Government’s ambitious agenda to build a resilient, inclusive, and digitally enabled nation.

The Maldives Digital Summit will bring together national leaders, international policymakers as well as global digital transformation experts to accelerate progress on key digital public infrastructure initiatives. The event is being held as part of the Digital Maldives for Adaptation, Decentralization and Diversification (DMADD) Project, supported by the World Bank, which aims to strengthen foundational digital systems critical for modern public service delivery. This includes foundational systems such as digital ID, data exchange platforms, and interoperable service delivery frameworks.

**Advancing Maldives 2.0 through Global Knowledge and Local Leadership**

The summit is designed to foster high-level dialogue and practical engagement on strengthening institutional coordination, modernizing public services, and enabling data-driven governance. Participants will explore global best practices and real-world experiences in designing, governing, and operationalizing Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), with a strong focus on citizen-centric outcomes.

Internationally renowned speakers will share lessons from leading digital governments, including

1. Mr. Iurie Turcanu, former Deputy Prime Minister for Digitalization, Moldova

2. Mr. Yoon-seok Ko, Vice President, National Information Society Agency, South Korea

3. Ms. Jessica McEvoy, former Programme Director, Government Digital Service, United Kingdom

**Key Focus Areas of the Summit**

Discussions and sessions throughout the event will focus on critical pillars of the Maldives’ digital transformation journey, including:

o Governance and Institutional coordination for digital transformation

o Secure and interoperable data sharing through a National Data Exchange Platform

o Citizen-centric service design to improve accessibility and efficiency

o Digital identity systems and trusted digital transactions, including eFaas

o Responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and emerging technologies

o Developing a clear and actionable implementation roadmap for Maldives 2.0 from Strategic Dialogue to Practical Implementation

**The three-day event is structured to ensure both strategic alignment and hands-on capacity building:**

o Day 1 – High-Level Summit (27 April 2026): Vision-setting and Strategic Dialogue, international country experiences, panel discussions, and thematic sessions aimed at senior decision-makers.

o Days 2–3 – Technical Workshops (28–29 April 2026): In-depth workshops covering citizen experience design, national data exchange platform implementation, digital identity enhancements, Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) and ID modernization, and interactive practical exercises.

**Strengthening Capacity and Partnerships**

The summit will convene senior government officials, digital transformation officers, technical agencies, international experts, development partners, and private sector stakeholders. Key participating institutions include the President’s Office, line ministries, Maldives Digital Service (MDS), MINDCo, the Department of National Registration (DNR), and World Bank representatives.

Expected outcomes of the Maldives Digital Summit include stronger alignment on the Maldives 2.0 implementation agenda, enhanced institutional capacity across government, a clearer roadmap for digital ID and data-sharing platforms, and strengthened partnerships with global digital leaders. The event will also help identify priority actions and next steps under the DMADD project.

**A Milestone for a Digital-First Maldives**

The Maldives Digital Summit underscores the Government’s continued commitment to transforming public service delivery through technology, innovation, and collaboration. By combining global expertise with national leadership, the summit aims to translate vision into action: laying the foundation for a resilient, data-driven, and citizen-centric digital future for the Maldives.

dv.title: މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަމިޓުގެ ނަމުގައި ސަމިޓެއް ބާއްވަނީ
dv.description: މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް (އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް) އާއި ވޯލްޑްބޭންކް ގުޅިގެން މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަމިޓެއް ބޭއްވުމަށް ތައްޔާރު ވެއްޖެއެވެ.
dv.body:
މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް (އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް) އާއި ވޯލްޑްބޭންކް ގުޅިގެން މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަމިޓެއް ބޭއްވުމަށް ތައްޔާރު ވެއްޖެއެވެ. މި ސަމިޓަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޑިޖިޓަލް ފަސްޓް ނޭޝަން ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަން އެޖެންޑާ ކުރިއަށް ގެންދިއުމުގެ މަޤްޞަދުގައި ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ސަމިޓެކެވެ. މި ސަމިޓް ބޭއްވުމަށް ތާވަލުކުރެވިފައިވަނީ މި ހިނގާ އޭޕްރީލް މަހުގެ 27 ން 29 އަށް ރާއްޖޭގެ މަޝްހޫރު ހޮޓަލެއްކަމުގައިވާ ބާސެލޯ ނަސަންދުރާ ހޮޓެލްގައެވެ. މި ސަމިޓް ބޭއްވުމަށް މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް އާއި ޑީމެޑް ޕްރޮޖެޓް ޓީމުން އެންމެ ފަހުގެ ތައްޔާރީތައް ވަމުން ދާއިރު، މި ސަމިޓަކީ މޯލްޑިވްސް 2.0 ގެ ރޯޑުމެޕްގައި ހިމެނޭ ހަރަކާތްތަކާއި، މޯލްޑިވްސް 2.0ގެ ވިޝަން ޙާޞިލުކުރުމަށްޓަކައި މުޙިއްމު ދައުރެއް އަދާކުރާނެ ސަމިޓެކެވެ.

މީގެ އިތުރުން މިސަމިޓަކީ ޑިޖިޓަލް ޕަބްލިކް އިންފްރާސްޓްރަކްޗަރ އިނީޝިއޭޓިވްތައް އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާ ކުރުމަށް ދުނިޔޭގެ ލީޑަރުންނާއި، ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ސިޔާސަތު ކަނޑައަޅާ ފަރާތްތަކާއި، ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަން އެކްސްޕާޓުން އެއްތަނަކުން ފެނިގެންދާނެ ސަމިޓެކެވެ.

އަދި މި ސަމިޓުގެ މައިގަޑު މަގްސަދުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި އިންސްޓިޓިއުޝަނަލް ކޯޑިނޭޝަން ހަރުދަނާ ކުރުމާއި، ޕަބްލިކް ސަރވިސަސް ޒަމާނީ ކުރުމާއި، ޑޭޓާ ޑްރައިވިން ގަވަރނަންސް ޤާއިމުކުރުމާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަތީ ފަންތީގެ މަޝްވަރާތައްކުރުން ހިމެނެއެވެ. މި ސަމިޓުގައި ބައިވެރިވާ ފަރާތްތަކުން ޑިޖިޓަލް ޕަބްލިކް އިންފްރާސްޓްރަކްޗަރ އާއި، ޑިޖިޓަލް ދައުލަތެއް ބިނާކުރުމާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން އަލިއަޅުވާލުމާއި ދުނިޔޭގެ އެންމެ ރަނގަޅު ގޮތްތަކާއި، ޙަޤީޤީ ދުނިޔޭގެ ތަޖުރިބާތައް ޙިއްޞާކުރުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ.

މި ސަމިޓުގައި ބައިވެރިވެ ވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ބައިނަލްއަޤުވާމީ ފެންވަރުގައި ފާހަގަކޮށްލެވޭ ކީ ނޯޓު ސްޕީކާރސް ތެރެގައި ހިމެނެނީ:

o މޮލްޑޯވަރގެ ޑިޖިޓަލައިޒޭޝަންގެ ފޯރމަރ ޕްރައިމް މިނިސްޓަރ މިސްޓަރ އިއުރީ ޓުރްކާނޯ،

o ސައުތު ކޮރެއާގެ ނޭޝަނަލް އިންފޮމޭޝަން ސޮސައިޓީ އޭޖެންސީގެ ވައިސް ޕްރެޒިޑެންޓް މިސްޓަރ ޔޫން ސިއޮކް ކޯ

o ޔޫކޭގެ ގަވަރމެންޓް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސްގެ ފޯރމަރ ޕްރޮގްރާމް ޑިރެކްޓަރ މިސް ޖެސިކާ މެކްއެވޮއީ.

**މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަމިޓުގެ މުޙިއްމު ބައިތައް**

މި ސަމިޓުގައި ރާއްޖޭގެ ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޯމޭޝަންގެ މުހިންމު އަސާސްތަކާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާ ކުރުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާއިރު، އޭގެ ތެރޭގައި ހިމެނެނީ:

o ގަވަރނަންސް އެންޑް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޝަނަލް ކޯޑިނޭޝަން ފޮރ ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަން އާއި ގުޅޭ ގޮތުން

o ނޭޝަނަލް ޑޭޓާ އެކްސްޗޭންޖް ޕްލެޓްފޯމް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ރައްކާތެރި އަދި އިންޓަރއޮޕަރަބަލް ޑޭޓާ ޝެއަރ ކުރުމާއި ގޮތުން

o ސިޓިޒަން ސެންޓްރިކް ސަރވިސް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން

o ޑިޖިޓަލް އައިޑެންޓިޓީ ސިސްޓަމް އާއި ޓްރަސްޓެޑް ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސެކްޝަންސް އާއި ގުޅޭ ގޮތުން

o އާޓިފިޝަލް އިންޓެލިޖެންސް (އޭއައި) އަދި ކުރިއަރަމުން އަންނަ ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީސްތައް ޒިންމާދާރު ގޮތުގައި ބޭނުން ކުރުމާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން

o މޯލްޑިވްސް 2.0 ގެ މަގުޗާޓުގައިވާ ހަރަކާތްތައް އިމްޕްލިމެންޓްކޮށް ތަރައްޤީ ކުރުމާއި ގުޅޭ ގޮތުން

**މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަމިޓު ކުރިއަށް ދާނެ ގޮތް**

o ދުވަސް 1: 27 އޭޕްރީލް 2026: ހައި ލެވަލް ސަމިޓް

o ދުވަސް 2 އަދި 3: 28 އަދި 29 އޭޕްރީލް 2026: ޓެކްނިކަލް ވާކްޝޮޕް

**މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަމިޓުގެ މުޙިއްމު ބައިވެރިން**

o ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީހާއި މިނިސްޓްރީތަކުގެ ސީނިއަރ އޮފިޝަލުން

o މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް (އެމް.ޑީ.އެސް)

o ވޯލްޑް ބޭންކް ރެޕްރެޒެންޓޭޓިވްސް

o މޯލްޑިވްސް އިނޮވޭޝަން އެންޑް ޑިޖިޓަލް ކޮމްޕެނީ (މައިންޑްކޯ)

o ޑިޕާޓްމެންޓް އޮފް ނޭޝަނަލް ރެޖިސްޓްރޭޝަން (ޑީ.އެން.އާރު)

o ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަން އޮފިސަރުން

o އިންޓަނޭޝަނަލް އެކްސްޕާޓުންނާއި ޕްރެކްޓިޝަނަރުން

o ޕަބްލިކް އަދި ޕްރައިވެޓް ސެކްޓަރ ސްޓޭކްހޯލްޑަރުން

featuredImage.alt: 23 Years of Service in the IT Sector Since the Establishment of the National Centre for Information Technology

en.title: 23 Years of Service in the IT Sector Since the Establishment of the National Centre for Information Technology
en.description: In the early 2000s, a master plan for science and technology was introduced which led to the establishment of the National Centre for Information Technology.
en.body: In the early 2000s, a master plan for science and technology was introduced which led to the establishment of the National Centre for Information Technology. In 2001, the National ICT Policy and the Science and Technology Master Plan were officially introduced. In 2002, a proposal was submitted to restructure the National Computer Centre to establish the NCIT. The announcement of the establishment of the National Centre for Information Technology on 25 March 2003 by the President's Office (Statement No: 26/2003) was the beginning of a revolutionary change in the IT sector. The National Centre for Information Technology (NCIT), which was established on March 25, 2003, completed 23 years on March 25, 2026. This Remarkable Year, the name of the National Centre for Information Technology was changed to Maldives Digital Service by the President's Office Statement (Reference No 2026/04) on 15 January 2026

dv.title: ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީ ވުޖޫދުވިތާ 23 އަހަރު ފުރުން
dv.description: މީލާދީ ސަނަތުން ދެހާހުގެ ކުރީ ކޮޅު ސައިންސް އެންޑް ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ މާސްޓަރ ޕްލޭނެއް ތަޢާރަފްކުރުމަށް މަސައްކަތްތަކެއް ކުރުން ވެގެން ދިއައީ މިހާރު މިދެކޭ "މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް" ނުވަތަ ކުރީގެ ނަމުން ނަމަ "ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ…
dv.body: މީލާދީ ސަނަތުން ދެހާހުގެ ކުރީ ކޮޅު ސައިންސް އެންޑް ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ މާސްޓަރ ޕްލޭނެއް ތަޢާރަފްކުރުމަށް މަސައްކަތްތަކެއް ކުރުން ވެގެން ދިއައީ މިހާރު މިދެކޭ "މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް" ނުވަތަ ކުރީގެ ނަމުން ނަމަ "ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީ" ވުޖޫދު ވުމަށް މެދުވެރިވި ސަބަބެއް ކަމުގައެވެ. މިގޮތުން 2001 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ ތެރޭގައި ރަސްމީކޮށް ނޭޝަނަލް އައިސީޓީ ޕޮލިސީ އަދި ސައިންސް އެންޑް ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ މާސްޓަރ ޕްލޭން ތަޢާރަފްކުރެވުނެވެ. އަދި ޖެހިގެން އައި 2002 ވަނަ އަހަރު އެން.ސީ.އައި.ޓީ ވުޖޫދުކުރުމަށްޓަކައި ނޭޝަނަލް ކޮމްޕިއުޓަރ ސެންޓަރ ރީސްޓްރަކްޗަރކުރުމުގެ ޕްރޮޕޯސަލް ހުށަހެޅުނެވެ. މިއާއެކު ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީހުގެ ނަންބަރު 26/2003 (23 އޭޕްރީލް 2003) ދެންނެވުމުން 2003 މާރިޗު 25 ވަނަ ދުވަހުން ފެށިގެން ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ ނަމުގައި އިދާރާއެއް އުފައްދައި، މި އިދާރާގެ އެންމެހާ ކަންތައްތައް ހިންގާނީ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ކޮމިއުނިކޭޝަން، ސައިންސް އެންޑް ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ ދަށުން ކަމުގައި ޢާންމުކޮށް އިޢުލާން ކުރުން ވެގެން ދިއައީ އައިޓީ ސެކްޓަރ އަށް އިންގިލާބީ ބަދަލެއް އައުމުގެ ފެށުން ކަމުގައެވެ. އަދި  2003 މާރިޗް 25 ވަނަ ދުވަހު ވުޖޫދުވި ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީ އަށް 2026 މާރިޗް 25 ގެ ނިޔަލަށް 23 އަހަރު ފުރިގެން މިދާ އަހަރަކީ މިއިދާރާގެ ނަން މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް އަށް ބަދަލުވި އަހަރުވެސް މެއެވެ. މިގޮތުން ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ ނަން މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް އަށް ބަދަލުވެފައިވަނީ މިއަހަރުގެ ޖެނުއަރީ 15 ވަނަ ދުވަހު ރައިސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީހުގެ ދެންނެވުން 2026/04 ނަންބަރ އިން ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީ އުވާލައްވައި މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސްގެ ނަމުގައި އިދާރާއެއް އުފެއްދުމާއި ގުޅިގެންނެވެ.

featuredImage.alt: President establishes Maldives Digital Service and abolishes National Centre for Information Technology

en.title: President establishes Maldives Digital Service and abolishes National Centre for Information Technology
en.description: President Dr Mohamed Muizzu has established the Maldives Digital Service under the administrative oversight of the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology, following the abolishment of the National Centre for Information Technology…
en.body:
President Dr Mohamed Muizzu has established the Maldives Digital Service under the administrative oversight of the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology, following the abolishment of the National Centre for Information Technology (NCIT).

The agency was established and the NCIT dissolved under Article 116(a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, with the decision communicated via a directive issued by the President's Office today.

This initiative aligns with the Cabinet's deliberations on 25 September 2025 regarding the Digital-First Nation vision. The agency is designated as the primary executive body responsible for implementing the Maldives 2.0 Roadmap 2025–2028: Journey to Digital Transformation.

The Maldives Digital Service will assume all responsibilities previously undertaken by the NCIT, in addition to spearheading implementation of the roadmap.

The number 1137 has been assigned for official correspondence with the agency, as per [Presidential Directive No. 4/2026.](https://presidency.gov.mv/Press/Article/36040)

dv.title: ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ، "މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް" އުފައްދަވައި، "ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީ" އުވައިލައްވައިފި
dv.description: ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑޮކްޓަރ މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު، "މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް" އުފައްދަވައި، އެއިދާރާއަކީ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ހޯމްލޭންޑް ސެކިއުރިޓީ އެންޑް ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ ދަށުން ހިންގާ ތަނެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ހަމަޖައްސަވައި "ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ…
dv.body:
ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑޮކްޓަރ މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު، "މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް" އުފައްދަވައި، އެއިދާރާއަކީ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ހޯމްލޭންޑް ސެކިއުރިޓީ އެންޑް ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ ދަށުން ހިންގާ ތަނެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ހަމަޖައްސަވައި "ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީ" މިއަދު އުވައިލައްވައިފިއެވެ. މިކަން ޢިއުލާންކުރެއްވީ މިއަދު ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީހުން ނެރުއްވި [ދެންނެވުމެއް](https://presidency.gov.mv/Press/Article/36040)ގައެވެ.

"މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް"ގެ ނަމުގައި އިދާރާއެއް މިއަދު އުފައްދަވައި، އެ އިދާރާއަކީ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ހޯމްލޭންޑް ސެކިއުރިޓީ އެންޑް ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީގެ ދަށުން ހިނގަމުންދާ ތަނެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ހަމަޖައްސަވައި، އެ މިނިސްޓްރީގެ ދަށުން ހިނގަމުންދިޔަ "ނޭޝަނަލް ސެންޓަރ ފޮރ އިންފޮމޭޝަން ޓެކްނޯލޮޖީ" މިއަދުން ފެށިގެން އުވައިލައްވާފައިވަނީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީގެ 116ވަނަ މާއްދާގެ (ހ)އިން ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއަށް ލިބިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ އިޚުތިޔާރުގެ ދަށުންނެވެ.

ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީހުން ނެރުއްވި ދެންނެވުމުގައި "މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް" އުފެއްދެވީ، ޑިޖިޓަލް-ފަސްޓް ނޭޝަން ތަސައްވުރާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން 2025 ސެޕްޓެންބަރު 25ވަނަ ދުވަހު ބޭއްވެވި ވަޒީރުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖަލްސާއަށް ހުށަހަޅުއްވައި މަޝްވަރާކުރައްވައިފައިވާ "މޯލްޑިވްސް 2.0 ރޯޑްމެޕް 2025-2028 - ޖަރނީ ޓު ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަން" މަގުޗާޓު ތަންފީޒުކުރުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން އެ މަޖިލީހުން ނިންމަވައިފައިވާ ނިންމެވުންތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި، "މޯލްޑިވްސް 2.0 ރޯޑްމެޕް 2025-2028 - ޖަރނީ ޓު ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަން" މަގުޗާޓުގައިވާ ކަންކަން ތަންފީޒުކުރުމުގެ ޒިންމާ ހަވާލުކުރާ އެންމެ އިސް އިދާރާއަކީ، މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް ކަމުގައި ހަމަޖެއްސެވުމަށް ނިންމަވައިފައިވާތީ ކަމުގައި ބަޔާންކުރައްވާފައިވެއެވެ.

މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސް އުފެއްދެވުމާ ގުޅިގެން، "މޯލްޑިވްސް 2.0 ރޯޑްމެޕް 2025-2028 - ޖަރނީ ޓު ޑިޖިޓަލް ޓްރާންސްފޮމޭޝަން" މަގުޗާޓުގައިވާ ކަންކަން ތަންފީޒުކުރުމުގެ ޒިންމާ އަދާކުރާ އެންމެ އިސް އިދާރާގެ ހައިސިއްޔަތުން ކުރައްވަންޖެހޭ މަސައްކަތްތަކުގެ އިތުރުން، އެން.ސީ.އައި.ޓީ.އިން މިހާތަނަށް ކުރައްވަމުން ގެންދެވި މަސައްކަތްތައް ކުރައްވަމުން ގެންދަވާނީވެސް، މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސްއިންނެވެ.

މޯލްޑިވްސް ޑިޖިޓަލް ސަރވިސްއަށް ދައުލަތުގެ އިދާރާތަކުން ލިޔުއްވާ ސިޓީގައި ޖައްސަވާނެ ނަންބަރަކީ 1137 ކަމުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީހުގެ ނަންބަރު 2026/4 ވަނަ [ދެންނެވުމުން](https://presidency.gov.mv/Press/Article/36040) މިއަދު ވަނީ އަންގަވާފައެވެ.
